summary: Revised the main question's account so it matches the evidence actually held: the Node-interface receipt is folded in (the same 1 -> 0 leader-context change observed on a real Node started by RestartNode, with the local-type control holding and Node.ForgetLeader producing the identical transition), which removes the last scope objection that this was a RawNode/harness artefact, and the joint history now covers five receipts of the same lineage. I also made the conditions the effect depends on explicit from source rather than implicit: the defeated lease test exists only with Config.CheckQuorum enabled, the type is a no-op on leaders so the incumbent keeps serving until it learns a higher term, and a candidate whose log is behind is still refused by isUpToDate. Severity bounds are unchanged (per-message effect, repair by the next leader message, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refusing the type, no committed-entry loss after the forged election). Validation passed with no execution requested; remaining work is scope-limited only — in-process hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, and no quantification of how long two leaders can overlap under delayed delivery.
